summary: Fixed a live reopen-after-broker-stop race in S007: decide() could still want a label the broker had already stopped out (its own M1-bar plan lagged the real tick-based fill by one cycle) and would attempt to re-place it with a now-invalid stop, saved only by luck when the broker rejected the order (TRADING_BAD_STOPS). Added StrategyLogger.label_was_opened() and made decide() backfill the close (reason=broker_side_close_detected) the same cycle it notices a previously-opened label missing from broker positions, instead of waiting for the next cycle to notice. Added regression tests covering both the new label_was_opened() method and the end-to-end decide() path.

Extracted the S007 decide()/reconcile logic out of bot/s007_paper.py::live() into a reusable run_cycle_for_account(creds, preset, risk_pct, fixed_lot, use_fixed_lot, magic, logger, ...) function, parameterized instead of hardcoded to bot.s007_config globals; live() now just calls it with the module defaults, so the single-account CLI behaviour is unchanged (verified via --dry-run regression). Rewrote webapp/runner.py for the new broker-agnostic multi-strategy schema (User/Account/AccountStrategy/Strategy) as a coordinator+worker pair: "python -m webapp.runner --strategy S007" loads enabled AccountStrategy rows and spawns one worker subprocess per account (because CTraderAdapter drives its session through a single reactor.run() call -- Twisted reactors cannot be restarted in the same process, so parallel accounts within one tick require one OS process each, not threads/asyncio); a worker runs exactly one cycle for one account_strategy id and exits. Curated events (cycle_start/cycle_end/position_open/position_close/error) now also write to the DB logs table via webapp/schemas/logs.py; full per-tick debug detail (and the label_was_opened/closed dedup state decide() depends on) still goes to per-account utils.trade_logger.StrategyLogger JSONL files under reports/logs/ -- NOT yet safe to drop for containerization, since that dedup state currently only lives in those files (open item). Rewrote webapp/cli.py for the same new schema (init-db/create-user/add-account/add-strategy/link-strategy/enable/disable/list), reusing webapp/schemas/ for validation. S009/Bybit multi-account support deliberately NOT done here: bot/s009_paper.py keeps its ledger state in one shared file for the whole strategy (load_state/save_state), not per (account, strategy), so it would need its own refactor before it could run several accounts in parallel the same way.

Added docs/DEV_PLANS.md, a new dev-plans doc capturing the decided multi-account Docker migration architecture (stateless-tick scheduling, per-strategy job granularity, DB-as-source-of-truth, DB schema decisions, logging split, Alembic migration convention, accounts.yml import mapping) and its current build status, so this is tracked in-repo instead of only in Claude memory. Linked it from README.md's docs/ listing.

Tested the new webapp.runner (coordinator+worker subprocess-per-account) end to end against the real DB-migrated S007/CTRADER account: coordinator found 1 enabled account_strategy row, spawned a worker, worker decrypted DB credentials, ran a full cTrader reconcile cycle, and wrote cycle_start/cycle_end to both the file logger and the DB logs table; account_strategies.status/last_cycle_at updated correctly. Uninstalled the old single-account launchd job (com.anton.algo.s007bot) now that the DB-driven runner path works. Two initial worker runs appeared to hang (55s+ with no output) -- root-caused to stdout full-buffering in a non-TTY subprocess hiding progress, combined with what looks like transient cTrader demo-server slowness, not a code bug: two subsequent clean runs completed in ~7s, matching the old single-account path.
CTraderS007.sync_snapshot(): one-session read-only snapshot of live positions + closing deals, for webapp/sync_positions.py.
details: Added a read-only snapshot call that opens ONE cTrader session and chains, via inlineCallbacks, _load_symbols -> _reconcile_step (ProtoOAReconcileReq) -> _deal_list_step (ProtoOADealListReq, N windows) -> _lot_sizes_step, then stops the reactor. One session because the demo server drops a fresh connection reconnected too soon after the previous one closed, so reconcile and deal-list cannot be two separate calls. Protocol constraints encoded here: (1) a single ProtoOADealListReq may not span more than a week, so the lookback is stitched from <=7-day windows; (2) money int64 fields are scaled by 10^moneyDigits which is PER-MESSAGE, not a constant, so each deal is scaled by its own message's moneyDigits; (3) executionPrice/entryPrice are plain doubles and must NOT be divided by PRICE_SCALE. Returns {'open': [{position_id,label,side,price,sl,tp,volume_lots}], 'deals': [...], 'lot_size': ...}. No orders are placed and nothing is modified at the broker.

summary: Surfaced S007 "ghost" trades: plan_now() now returns reached_tp/n_recovery in context and a new resolved list of positions the engine entered AND resolved (stop/tp/daycap) within the same replayed bars -- these never reach the broker because decide() only places orders for still-open ('eod') positions, so previously they left no trace at all. decide() now logs each first-seen resolved position via a new StrategyLogger.label_was_ghosted()-guarded position(label, "ghost", ...) call. Investigated live 2026-08-05: a B setup formed and resolved before any cycle saw it as open; a historical replay of the events log (2026-08-01 through 2026-08-05) found 2 prior days (08-01, 08-03) with the same pattern -- a scenario detected, n_desired never above 0, no order ever placed -- newly distinguishable from a normal no-signal day now that this is logged.

Fixed a live order-placement bug found while checking today's S007 logs: every cycle since 10:03 today (2026-08-06) rejected with INVALID_REQUEST "Order price ... has more digits than symbol allows" (e.g. 26081.200000000004 for a DE40 symbol that only accepts 2 decimals) -- sl_price/tp_price flow through several float ops (range mid, swing stops) on quotes with up to 5 decimals (PRICE_SCALE), so an unrounded value routinely picks up float noise past the symbol precision. _place_market_step now rounds both to full_symbol.digits (already fetched per cycle for sizing) before sending. No dedicated regression test added yet -- would need the fake-SDK harness in tests/bot/test_check_response.py, which currently fails at collection for an unrelated reason (ctrader_s007 import error), not investigated further here.

Fixed two problems in this test file found while checking today's trading logs. (1) Its autouse _clean_position_log fixture was shutil.rmtree()-ing the REAL reports/logs/S007/positions/ directory before/after every test (not a tmp dir) -- running this file while the live launchd tick (com.anton.algo.s007bot) happened to be mid-cycle deleted all production per-position history and threw a FileNotFoundError in that live cycle (incident 2026-08-06, see decisions-log.md; no data was actually lost, since every position/order event is duplicated into reports/logs/S007/events-<date>.jsonl, untouched by this). Replaced it with monkeypatch.setattr(s007_paper, 'LOG', StrategyLogger("S007TEST", log_root=str(tmp_path))) -- same per-test isolation guarantee, zero risk to real data. (2) The 4 tests mocking plan_now via lambda m1: ... had been broken (TypeError: unexpected keyword argument preset) since the 2026-07-31 run_cycle_for_account refactor added preset=preset to the real call site without updating these mocks; widened the lambda signature to lambda m1, preset=None: .... All 17 tests in the file (plus test_s007_signals.py and test_label_was_closed.py) pass now.

Fixed a second live order-placement bug found today (2026-08-06), right after the price-rounding one: a b-reversal leg is simulated against its own target (tp_A, the opposite range boundary) via _simulate_leg(...tp_A...), but engine.py never stored that per-leg tp on the position dict, and s007_signals.py::plan_now built every wanted positions tp from the single day-level r["tp"] (the PRIMARY B legs target). Live: a reversal BUY went out with the original SELL legs (lower) target attached and cTrader rejected it outright (TRADING_BAD_STOPS: New TP for BUY pending order should be > entry price), repeating every cycle for labels :93/:114/:117 from 11:38 onward, following the same pattern as the earlier :1/:13/:38 sequence. Fix: _simulate_leg now stores tp=tp on every position dict it creates (both the initial entry and pyramided adds); plan_now uses each positions own p["tp"] instead of the shared day-level tp when building wanted/resolved. Verified against the real 2026-06-17 B-stopped/A-reversal-hit-tp historical day (same one used for the ghost-trade fix): the still-open reversal leg now reports tp=24818.666 (rl, correct) instead of 25110.899 (the primary legs tp, which was invalid on the reversal sellside too). Added a regression test asserting a wanted positions tp differs from the day-level context tp and is on the correct side of its own entry.

Generalized webapp/runner.py's strategy dispatch from a hardcoded S007-only check to a STRATEGY_WORKERS registry ({'S007': _worker_s007, 'S009': _worker_s009}), and refactored bot/s009_paper.py so S009 can run multi-account through it: extracted run_cycle_for_account(account_key, creds, state, logger, ...) from run_once()'s body (mirrors bot/s007_paper.py's function of the same name/shape), parameterized by an injectable state store instead of the single global reports/paper_s009/state.json. Added migration 003 (strategy_state table, one JSON blob per account_strategy_id) + webapp/state_store.py::DBStateStore for the DB-driven path, and utils/strategy_state.py::FileStateStore (extracted load_state/save_state) for the unchanged single-account CLI path -- run_once()/--status/--loop/scripts/s009_tick.py keep writing the same file, byte-for-byte, verified via a real --status read after the refactor. _worker_s009 hardcodes broker='off'/allow_mainnet=False deliberately -- enabling real orders through the DB-driven path is a separate future decision, not a side effect. Verified end-to-end against a throwaway copy of the real DB: `webapp.runner --worker --account-strategy-id 3` (Bybit-algo009) correctly wrote a strategy_state row and updated account_strategies.status, with zero broker orders. 55 new+existing tests pass (10 bot, 13 webapp, 32 scripts).

Stopped the S009 test suite from writing into the LIVE paper ledger. run_cycle_for_account() books each closed day via append_ledger(), which resolves LEDGER_FILE/STATE_DIR from bot/s009_paper.py module globals; only one of the eleven tests (test_run_once_uses_the_module_level_state_store) patched them, so every other test that booked a day appended fake rows straight into reports/paper_s009/ledger.csv. Three such rows (day 20001, 2024-10-05, net_ret 0.02, equity 1.02) were found in the live file on 2026-08-08, written after the bot had already booked two real days -- they corrupt the only record of live performance and are exactly what --reconcile reads. Added a module-level autouse fixture _isolate_paper_dirs(tmp_path, monkeypatch) that repoints REPO/STATE_DIR/STATE_FILE/LEDGER_FILE at a temp dir for every test, mirroring the S007 positions-log cleanup fixture (decisions-log 2026-07-21). The three fake rows were removed from the live ledger (backup kept as reports/paper_s009/ledger.csv.bak-20260808-testrows); the two genuine days (2026-08-06 +1.2445%, 2026-08-07 -0.7597%, equity 1.004753) are intact and match state.json. Verified without pytest (unavailable on this bridge VM) by replaying the fixture and the stubbed engine manually and forcing the booking path with last_day = FAKE_DAY - 1: two days booked, both rows landed in the temp ledger, and the real ledger stayed byte-identical (sha256 27dd6a32... before and after). NOT fixed, reported separately: append_ledger() still writes to one global ledger regardless of account_key, so the DB-driven multi-account path would mix every account's equity curve into one file -- the per-account state store has no ledger counterpart.

Fixed a real collision left over from the S009 multi-account refactor: append_ledger() still wrote the module-global LEDGER_FILE regardless of which `state` store was passed to run_cycle_for_account(), so even after state.json was made per-account (DBStateStore), every account's day_pnl rows would still land in the SAME shared reports/paper_s009/ledger.csv -- exactly the collision that refactor was supposed to eliminate. Found because a test run of tests/bot/test_s009_paper.py (before this fix) wrote fake rows into the real live ledger; someone/something added an _isolate_paper_dirs autouse fixture there as a stopgap, which stays. Root-caused and fixed properly: run_cycle_for_account() now takes an explicit ledger_file=None param and only calls append_ledger() when one is given; run_once()'s single-account CLI path passes its own LEDGER_FILE (unchanged behavior, regression-tested), while the DB-driven multi-account path (_worker_s009) deliberately passes none and relies solely on the already-per-account StrategyLogger day_pnl events instead. append_ledger()'s own default was changed from a bound `= LEDGER_FILE` parameter (captured once at def-time, invisible to test monkeypatching) to a None-sentinel resolved fresh on every call. Also added S009 to deployment/schedule.yml (once daily, '5 0 * * *' UTC, not every-minute like S007: run_cycle_for_account has no cheap already-up-to-date short-circuit, so frequent scheduling would hit Bybit's public API for nothing; still broker='off' hardcoded, no orders regardless of cadence). Verified end-to-end against a throwaway migrated copy of the real DB: scripts/scheduler_tick.py correctly dispatched only S009 (not S007) at a simulated 00:05 UTC Monday, wrote strategy_state, zero broker orders.

Fixed a real-money bug found while checking bot status: run_cycle_for_account() constructed BybitExec without ever passing env, so it always fell back to the BYBIT_TESTNET OS env var -- unset in the Ofelia dispatch container (not in docker-compose.ymls environment list, and .env is deliberately excluded from the image per .dockerignore with a since-stale bind-mount comment that was never implemented). Result: every DB-driven S009 cycle for Bybit-algo009 (a real-money MAINNET account, broker_mode=execute) silently hit api-testnet.bybit.com with its mainnet-only API key, 401ing (API key is invalid) and completely failing the cycle -- no rebalance, no equity read, nothing -- for about 17h (2026-08-13 21:05 UTC through 2026-08-14 14:xx UTC when this was caught), even though _worker_s009 already computed allow_mainnet from acc.env correctly (that only gates ORDER PLACEMENT, not which base URL/credential namespace BybitExec talks to). Added env: str | None = None to run_cycle_for_account, threaded through to both BybitExec(...) constructor call sites, and _worker_s009 now passes env=acc.env. Added regression tests in both tests/bot/test_s009_paper.py and tests/webapp/test_runner_s009.py (the existing allow_mainnet-focused tests never asserted on env at all -- confirmed both new tests fail against the pre-fix code and pass after). Rebuilt algo-worker, manually ran python -m webapp.runner --strategy S009 in-container to verify live: broker env=mainnet equity=102.48 mode=execute, caught up the missed 2026-08-13 day (net_ret=+1.6%), placed 4 of 6 real orders (2 rejected on a pre-existing, unrelated Bybit $5-minimum-order-value issue, not touched here). account_strategy id=3 status is now clean (no last_error).

While reviewing the S009/Bybit-algo009 portfolio, root-caused the recurring TRADING error 110094 (minimum order value 5USDT) on TRXUSDT/NEARUSDT seen on both 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-14: Bybit instruments-info exposes minNotionalValue (a $5 dollar-value floor) separately from minOrderQty (a unit-count floor) in lotSizeFilter, but Instrument/reconcile_to_target only ever checked minOrderQty. For these two legs a rebalancing DELTA easily clears minOrderQty (TRX min_qty=1 unit =~ $0.33, NEAR min_qty=0.1 =~ $0.16) while still being worth under $5, so a doomed order got submitted and rejected by Bybit every time instead of being recognized as too small to matter. Turned out NOT to be missing legs -- checked live broker positions directly: all 4 legs (TRX 101, BCH 0.17, SUI -50, NEAR -21) are near target weight (~0.339 each), the failures were just small day-to-day drift adjustments hitting the floor. Added Instrument.min_notional (read from lotSizeFilter.minNotionalValue, default 0.0 for categories/symbols that dont report it) and extended reconcile_to_target to skip (with a clear skip_min_qty log) instead of submit-and-fail when either floor isnt cleared. 3 new tests (bot/tests/bot/test_s009_paper.py) verified red on pre-fix code, green after. Rebuilt the image; live portfolio as of this check: equity $102.48 mainnet, roughly balanced 2-long/2-short book (~$34 notional each leg), state-tracked shadow equity +1.62% cumulative.

Documented (no behavior change) a live incident 2026-08-31 10:03 Kyiv: a B-down setup live order used entry=26440.6 (from the M1 bar closed only 4s earlier) with tp=26442.6, rejected by cTrader (TRADING_BAD_STOPS: TP must be < entry on a SELL). The 10:05 cycle re-scanned with 2 more bars and resolved the same setup already-tp'd at a different bar (entry=26469.1), consistent with the freshly-closed bar not having fully settled broker-side at query time. Unlike bot/s009_paper.py's drop_forming, nothing in run_live_cycle/find_setup excludes the most-recently-closed M1 bar. Not a regression of the 2026-08-06 (wrong per-leg tp) or 2026-08-13 (missing tp=tp on recovery leg) bugs -- both n_recovery=0 and the day-level tp were correct here. Even a fix likely would not have caught this specific trade live: by 10:05 the whole entry->TP move had already happened within already-elapsed bars, same class as the ghost-trade/1-minute-poll limitation behind promoting WORKING_S007_LIQFLOOR (decisions-log.md 2026-08-11/12). Added an in-code comment at the M1 fetch site in run_live_cycle recording this; no fix applied -- touching find_setup's bar window is a signal-engine behavior change needing backtest validation (Gate 0/1) first, and even so may not change the practical outcome. Anton chose to document only, not file a ticket or change behavior, this session.

ALGODEV-35: added liquidity_tp_ceiling_points (StrategyConfig) and wired it into engine.py::liquidity_tp -- caps a liquidity TP that lies beyond range_tp at range_tp+/-N points, on top of the existing liquidity_tp_floor (ALGODEV-21) which only stops a target being NEARER than range_tp. Prompted by a live 2026-09-02 case (Anton): a real S007 cycle picked liquidity 285.9pt beyond range_tp for its TP. Added 6 named presets (WORKING_S007_LIQCEIL10/20/30/40/50/100, all WORKING_S007_LIQFLOOR + a ceiling) and backtest/run_s007_liqceiling.py sweeping all 6 against uncapped LIQFLOOR at Gate 1 (gross) and Gate 2 (real spread 0.635/side) on the same 2026-08-11 Dukascopy refresh run_s007_liqfloor.py used -- confirmed a byte-matching regression against that script before trusting the new numbers. Verdict: REJECTED, all six. Gate 2 net R/day for ceil10..100 = +0.676/+0.687/+0.729/+0.784/+0.833/+0.837 vs uncapped LIQFLOORs +0.801 -- every ceiling <=40pt is worse (lower net, often deeper maxDD, e.g. ceil20/30 -65R vs -50.9R) despite a higher day win-rate (61-63% vs 60%); ceil50/100 approach uncapped but do not beat it (ceil100s maxDD is identical to uncapped, i.e. the cap essentially never binds there). Conclusion baked into the preset comments: distant liquidity targets that look alarming on any single day are net CONTRIBUTORS to the 3+-year edge, not noise -- capping them tighter loses profitability. WORKING_S007_LIQFLOOR (uncapped) stays the live preset; nothing promoted. default liquidity_tp_ceiling_points=None preserves byte-identical behavior for every existing preset (confirmed via the existing S007 test suite, 62 passed).

Day-scoped S007 risk caps after the 2026-09-02 incident (8 positions / ~-$401 / ~4% on a 2% cap day): both day caps in bot/s007_paper.py::decide were computed from the broker's open-positions snapshot, so every stop-out wave zeroed its own spent risk and the next wave got a fresh budget. Fix: (1) count cap now runs against opened_today_count -- every label our own append-only position log opened today (new StrategyLogger.open_records(prefix) in utils/trade_logger.py), union the live snapshot; (2) the $ gate now checks spent_risk_today = open_risk (broker fill/stop, unchanged) + closed-today risk at ACTUAL fill price, matched by position_id (now logged on the open record, extracted from ORDER_ACCEPTED) to the broker's last-24h closing deals -- run_live_cycle (bot/ctrader_s007.py) fetches _deal_list_step once per cycle in the same session and passes closed_deals into decide() (kwarg, default None -- old callers/fakes unaffected); planned-entry fallback when no deal matches, deal fetch failure falls back to [] and never kills the cycle. Slippage-inflated fills therefore keep counting at real size after closing. state/skip events now log spent_risk_today/closed_risk_today/opened_today. Replay of 2026-09-02's 8 opens vs the new gates: blocked from position 4 (10:57), day capped at ~-$194 spent of a $204 cap instead of -$401. Tests: 2 new in tests/bot/test_s007_live_sizing.py (stop-out waves; slipped fills from deal history incl. no-deals fallback); tests/bot/test_check_response.py SDK stub taught ProtoOADealListReq/ProtoOADealStatus (pre-existing breakage from the earlier deal-history import). Full run: 178 passed (tests/bot+utils+scripts+webapp).

ALGODEV-37 'maximally prop' scheme implemented AND cut over live (Anton's explicit decision: full switch, no parallel demo track). (1) New preset WORKING_S007_NEWSSAFE_MAX8_BE05 = NEWSSAFE_MAX8.with_(breakeven_at_r=0.5) -- verified dataclass-equal to run_s007_propscheme.py's winning ad-hoc combo (Gate 3: 100.0% cashout / 0.0% daily-bust). (2) Live breakeven: ProtoOAAmendPositionSLTPReq wired into bot/ctrader_s007.py (_amend_position_sltp_step, standalone amend_position_sl, 'amend' action kind in run_live_cycle using full_symbol.digits rounding). Trigger is the ENGINE's own be_moved flag surfaced through plan_now() (bot/s007_signals.py) -- same code path as the backtest, live/backtest can never disagree on WHEN; the amend targets the broker's ACTUAL fill price (have[lab]['price']) so real breakeven includes slippage; current takeProfit is always passed back because the amend message REPLACES both protection levels (unset TP would strip it). One-shot without extra state: decide() only amends when the current broker SL is strictly worse than the fill (buy: cur_sl<fill, sell: cur_sl>fill), so successful amends and manually-tightened stops are natural no-ops; failed amends retry next cycle. (3) FROZEN INVARIANT preserved (Anton: 'this must not break'): the 2026-09-02 day-cap fix untouched -- amends bypass opened_today/spent_risk_today accounting entirely, BE'd position still counts in the count cap; dedicated test. (4) webapp/runner.py taught the amend kind (previously everything non-open routed into _close_position_db -- an amend would have closed the DB row) + LogKind.POSITION_AMENDED. (5) Cutover: bot/s007_config.py PRESET -> WORKING_S007_NEWSSAFE_MAX8_BE05 AND EXIT_END '16:59' -> '14:24' -- CRITICAL PAIRING: plan_now() overrides the preset's session fields with s007_config values, a preset-only switch silently keeps trading to 16:59; DB (data/app.db): strategies.default_preset updated, link id=1 risk_pct 0.5 -> 0.25 (link currently enabled=0 -- re-enabling is Anton's call, NOT done this session); deployment/schedule.yml comment refreshed (cron window deliberately wider than EXIT_END). (6) Margin: new read-only scripts/check_s007_margin_8slots.py (ProtoOAExpectedMarginReq) run against the live demo -- 8 slots ~26.9% of balance, comfortable. FILL_PROB=0.75 confirmed ~0.735 empirically (prior session). Smoke: plan_now BE == engine BE on last 60 Dukascopy days (8/31 positions BE'd, all sl==entry; base preset never flags). Tests: 4 new in tests/bot/test_s007_live_breakeven.py; test_check_response SDK stub taught ProtoOAAmendPositionSLTPReq (fixes the 6 pre-existing errors); full run 149 passed. Docs: Jira ALGODEV-37 comment, Confluence S007 page 622593 v4 (status section) + work journal 10584066 v4, bot/S007_README.md.

Fixed a real-$ reporting bug in S009 found live 2026-09-03: run_cycle_for_account read the previous broker-ledger row via _last_broker_ledger_row(broker_ledger_file) even when broker_ledger_file was None (the DB-driven multi-account caller, webapp/runner.py::_worker_s009, always leaves it None by design). Unlike append_broker_ledger, which already skips writing when None, the read had no such guard and silently fell back to the single-account BROKER_LEDGER_FILE constant -- last written 2026-08-11 by the legacy single-account CLI before the 2026-08-13 DB migration. Every DB-driven cycle since then computed real_net_ret/hours_since_prev against that ~3-week-stale row instead of not reporting them at all (confirmed live: todays cycle logged hours_since_prev=550.31, exactly the gap from 2026-08-11 to now). Fix: guard the read the same way the write already is (broker_ledger_file is not None), so the DB-driven path now correctly logs real_net_ret/hours_since_prev as None rather than a number computed against an unrelated stale reading. Trading/order logic itself was never affected -- only this diagnostic metric. Added a regression test (test_no_ledger_file_ignores_a_stale_shared_broker_ledger) that pre-seeds a stale BROKER_LEDGER_FILE and asserts the logged broker event stays None when no broker_ledger_file is passed; verified it fails against the pre-fix code and passes after.

ALGODEV-38: fixed a live bug where decide() could place a BRAND NEW S007 position with sl==entry (zero stop distance) -- found live 2026-09-03, recurred twice same session, second time also silently bypassing the day risk cap (new_risk computed from stop_distance collapsed to 0). Root cause: plan_now() replays the whole days bars every cycle, so a late-detected reversal/add leg can already show be_moved=True (engine moved p["stop"]=p["entry"] via its breakeven rule) on the very first cycle it appears as wanted, even though it was never actually open at the broker before -- decide()s place branch used that already-moved stop verbatim. Fix: bot/s007_signals.py::plan_now now also returns orig_sl per position (rederived from risk0, which the breakeven block never mutates); bot/s007_paper.py::decide()s place branch uses o.get("orig_sl", o["sl"]) instead of o["sl"] for both the risk-cap stop_distance calc and the placed orders sl. The existing amend path (ALGODEV-37) is unchanged -- it still moves the broker real stop to breakeven from the actual fill price once a position is genuinely open. Added test_fresh_placement_uses_orig_sl_not_an_already_be_moved_sl (tests/bot/test_s007_live_sizing.py), verified it fails pre-fix and passes post-fix. Filed as Jira ALGODEV-38 (bug), moved to In Progress, fix + verification commented there. Full suite (tests/bot+webapp+utils+scripts) 183 passed + the new one; ruff clean. One unrelated pre-existing failure noted (tests/scripts/test_s007_tick.py::test_in_session_true_at_exit_end_hour, stale against an earlier uncommitted EXIT_END 16:59->14:24 change), not fixed here. NOT yet deployed: bot/ is baked into algo-worker:latest, not bind-mounted, so an image rebuild + Ofelia restart is still needed before this reaches the live DB-driven S007 worker.

Added a sequential pipeline (e2e) test suite for S007: a stateful fake cTrader broker (fills, server-side SL/TP execution, deal history) drives the REAL engine (simulate_day) through the REAL live wiring (plan_now -> decide -> run_cycle_for_account -> webapp.runner._worker_s007/DB) cycle-by-cycle across a simulated trading day, instead of each layer being tested in isolation against a hand-scripted stub of the layer below. Covers 35 cases across three catalogs: engine/signal shapes (A1-A15, e.g. A/B scenarios, b_reversal_to_A, breakeven, EOD flatten, ghost trades), decide()/sizing/day-cap wiring (B1-B20, e.g. risk sizing, min-lot floor overshoot, day count/$ caps, slippage-aware risk accounting, manual stop, broker/session error isolation), and the DB-driven runner (C1-C6, e.g. Position row lifecycle, settled-status stamping, multi-account cap isolation). No production code was changed; two informational (non-bug) findings were noted for a human to review: engine day_done tracks only the primary leg's target, not a winning recovery leg, and a very low daily_risk_cap_pct/risk_pct ratio floors max_positions_per_day to 0, masking the $ cap check behind the count cap.

ALGODEV-39 follow-up: a fresh S007 placement now captures the broker real fill price/stop via one extra reconcile right after placing (CTraderS007.run_live_cycle post_positions), and s007_paper.py.run_cycle_for_account logs/returns that real entry/sl (feeding the position log, the day-cap fallback math, and the DB Position row via webapp/runner.py) instead of the engine planned values. Planned values are kept alongside as planned_entry/planned_sl for diagnosability. Does not yet fix the breakeven TRIGGER itself (still engine-only, ALGODEV-39 core issue) -- this only fixes what gets recorded as the position entry/sl at open time. Added regression test test_fresh_placement_logs_the_real_broker_fill_not_the_planned_entry.

ALGODEV-39 core fix: the live breakeven trigger in decide() now ALSO fires off the broker real fill price/stop and the active preset breakeven_at_r (surfaced by plan_now() as breakeven_at_r), checked against M1 bars since the position real open time (opened_ts) -- not only the engine be_moved flag, which is blind to entry slippage and could leave a slipped position without breakeven protection near its real stop. Either trigger path firing is sufficient; the engine path is unchanged for the base near-zero-slippage case. Guarded to short-circuit before touching broker-position fields when neither trigger can possibly apply (breakeven off and engine has not fired), preserving prior behavior/test fixtures exactly. Falls back to checking only the latest bar (not the whole day) when opened_ts is unavailable, to avoid false-triggering off pre-open price history. Added regression tests test_amend_fires_off_real_fill_when_engine_be_moved_is_still_false and test_no_amend_when_real_price_has_not_reached_real_breakeven_yet.

ALGODEV-40 fix: orig_sl (ALGODEV-38) used to re-derive the pre-breakeven stop as entry -+ risk0 (direction-based), silently mirroring it to the wrong side whenever a pyramided add under stop_mode=mid_range has its entry beyond the legs shared stop -- a normal, expected geometry for this pyramiding style, not an edge case. Found live 2026-09-07: two adds (S007:2026-09-07:112, :135) got a wrong-side, too-tight stop sent to the broker and turned engine-validated wins (R=+1.0 each per independent replay on real M1 bars) into real losses (-.17, -.15, ~70% of that days -.47 net loss). Full audit of every real placement since the ALGODEV-38 fix went live (2026-09-03 11:26) confirmed exactly these 2 of 8 placements were affected, no other days. Fixed by having strategies/ger40_lonfra/engine.py::_simulate_leg store stop0 (the real, un-mutated creation-time stop) on every position dict alongside risk0, and having bot/s007_signals.py::plan_now surface stop0 directly as orig_sl instead of re-deriving it. Added 3 regression tests. Deployed via podman compose build worker ahead of the 2026-09-08 session open.
